recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what parallel planes share, and what changes between them.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the parallel-plane form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Parallel planes share a normal, so the new plane keeps the SAME coefficients — only its constant changes. The point-form a(x−x₁) + b(y−y₁) + c(z−z₁) = 0 does both at once.
steps.memory_tip: Same normal means same coefficients. a(x−x₁) + b(y−y₁) + c(z−z₁) = 0 does both jobs at once.
lines: Here, (x₁, y₁, z₁) = (1, 2, −3) and a = 2, b = −3, c = 6
The equation of the plane passing through (x₁, y₁, z₁) and parallel to the plane
a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) + c(z − z₁) = 0

recall.must_convey: That parallel planes share coefficients, so the point-form a(x−x₁)+b(y−y₁)+c(z−z₁)=0 is used.
accept: parallel planes have the same coefficients so only the constant changes
use a into x minus x one plus b into y minus y one plus c into z minus z one equals zero
keep the coefficients and put the point in
heard_as: a into x minus x one

steps.why: Two planes are parallel exactly when their normals point the same way, and the normal is carried by the coefficients — so keeping them is the whole condition.
common_mistakes: Changing a coefficient, which tilts the plane.
Using the original constant d, which reproduces the SAME plane rather than a parallel one.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put the given point and coefficients in, expand, and collect the constants.
steps.memory_tip: Watch the point's negative coordinate: z − (−3) becomes z + 3.
